evidence: Schema v7 adds append-only ledger events, normalized entities and relations, checkpoints, and explicit legacy bridges with project/time/type/subject/correlation/entity/relation indexes and mutation-denial triggers. Aggregate revision creation writes its portable T01 provenance record, normalized projections, chain checkpoint, narrow audit event, and outbox notification in one SQLite transaction; an injected late outbox failure rolls all of them back.

Retry joins on the governed ledger idempotency fingerprint and returns the exact prior revision only when the stored transaction is complete. It fails closed for an incomplete legacy outbox instead of synthesizing lineage or duplicating canonical output.

Bounded ancestor and descendant traversal verifies canonical record bytes, event denormalization, normalized entities and relations, hash-chain links, and checkpoints; missing immutable revision references or mismatches place the repository in integrity-review while retaining bounded read-only results. Queries expose producing activity and responsible agent without returning raw research content.

The exact-commit 100-test run covers successful persistence and lineage plus material failure, denial, rollback, replay, restart, migration, corruption, missing-reference, depth/cursor/page limit, and packaging boundaries.

Migration tests exercise fresh v7 creation and backup-first upgrade from historical schemas, including a real v6 fixture. Repository tests prove no canonical revision survives without its ledger, no ledger survives without its canonical revision, repeated requests are idempotent, and later integrity faults cannot be mistaken for valid lineage.
No test was removed or weakened; quality, public API generation, architecture, repository structure, backlog integrity, approved-W1 readiness, and the real Windows sidecar boundary pass.

Core API OpenAPI and generated TypeScript now include POST /projects/provenance/lineage with bounded ancestor/descendant, activity, and agent results. The additive v7 migration creates a pre-migration backup before mutation, verifies the resulting schema, and bridges historical narrow audit rows through explicit compatibility records without reinterpreting them as complete portable provenance. Post-v7 narrow events are bridged only when no portable ledger event already represents the transaction.
